title: A plugin loader
description:
Load small plugins, each in its own environment, and let them register commands.

```
loaded plugin "greet" (1 command)
loaded plugin "dice" (1 command)
plugin "broken" failed: [string "broken"]:1: syntax error near 'is'
> greet Ada  -> Hello, Ada!
> roll       -> 4
```

starter.main.lua:
local plugins = {
  greet = [[command("greet", function(who) return "Hello, " .. who .. "!" end)]],
  dice = [[command("roll", function() return math.random(1, 6) end)]],
  broken = [[this is not lua]],
}
local commands = {}

local function load_plugin(name, code)
  return false, "not written yet"
end

for name, code in pairs(plugins) do
  print(load_plugin(name, code))
end

hints: Make a new `env` table for each plugin, so their globals stay apart (lesson 7.01).
`env.command = function(cmd, fn) commands[cmd] = fn end` lets plugins register without seeing `commands` itself.
requirements: Each plugin is a string of Lua code run with `load(code, name, "t", env)`.
`env` has a `command(name, fn)` function, `print`, `math` and `string`, and nothing else.
A plugin that fails to load or run is reported and skipped.
Commands from one plugin cannot see another plugin's globals.
stretch: Unload a plugin: remember which commands came from which plugin and remove them.
